notes:
Summary: Lost procurement to competitor (OpenAI + vendor-managed tool orchestration). Primary reason: observed quality regressions in Redwood's model behavior during the production-like POC versus incumbent. Customer: platform for automated conversational workflows across order management and refunds; strict schema / tool-calling correctness required.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-10-03: Lead created via webinar. Intro call (AE Jordan Kim + SE Anika Rao).
- 2025-11-12: POC kickoff (scope: support chat + automated order adjuster with function calls to internal order API).
- 2025-12-07: Mid-POC technical review (SE demoed structured JSON output validation harness).
- 2026-01-05: POC stress run against subset of live traffic (10k msgs). Observed failure modes captured.
- 2026-02-10: Final demo; procurement discussion. Customer indicated they were consolidating vendors.

POC findings (customer-facing, bullets):
- Redwood: excellent latency profile and cost estimates on dedicated pool; autoscaling looked good.
- Major blocker: structured output reliability — Redwood model produced valid JSON schema only ~82% of runs under noisy prompts. Incumbent reported >95% on same harness.
- Tool-calling reliability: in 6% of test flows Redwood produced malformed args or incorrect enum values causing remote API failures. Incumbent's tool-calling abstraction (wrapper + prompt-tuning) had fewer regressions in our tests.
- Edge-case handling: when fallback to alternative model variant occurred, the schema shape changed (keys reordered/missing) breaking downstream idempotency checks.
- Customer quote (POC CDM): "We can't automate order changes unless the agent's tool calls are deterministic and schema-correct — false positives cause refunds."

Security/compliance items:
- Customer requires SOC2 Type II and SAML SSO; Redwood provided SOC2 report but customer wants an in-contract attestation and a SOC2 of the Dedicated region.
- Data residency: legal prefers EU residency for EU customers; Veridian's EU region mix required contractual guarantees.
- Consequence: security team put purchase on hold, asked for additional attestation and penetration test results.

Commercial / org dynamics:
- Buying committee split: Product (owns UX), Ops (owns runbooks & reliability), Legal/Security (procurement gate). No single champion — previous champion promoted out during procurement window.
- Finance imposed a Q1 hiring freeze → hold on new SOWs.

Competitive dynamics and why lost:
- Customer selected competitor because of stronger out-of-the-box tool-calling consistency and an existing enterprise contract (volume discount + managed wrapper for function calls).
- Competitor offered a short-term migration plan and pay-for-quality SLA that matched customer's risk tolerance.

Internal notes / follow-ups:
- SE notes: failure analysis attached in Drive (parsing-harness results, sample payloads, failure-rate breakdown). Actionable: invest in structured-output prompt templates + schema-constrained decoders; add deterministic post-processing validators to Redwood SDK and demo again.
- Product ask: add a feature brief on "schema-safe generation + function call hardening" for mid-market verticals.
- Growth ask: create a pricing skus doc for small-mid SOWs that includes remediation credits for quality regressions.

Next steps (CRM):
- Mark as closed-lost in CRM; reason = quality_regression_vs_incumbent + budget_freeze + security_timing.
- Sequence: pause outreach for 90 days; schedule check-in for 2026-05 if SOC2 attestation issued or budget reopens.
- Follow-up owner: Jordan Kim to keep notification email for SOC2/pen-test completions.

Attachments / artifacts:

- Security Q&A (legal): thread-CA+2110_security-questions.
